summary: Scarlett J. He works in Tibetology and history and archaeology. A doctoral student at Columbia University (attested 2026), she also holds a post there.

Schuyler Cammann (1912–1991) was a scholar in Sinology, Tibetology, and history and archaeology. Educated at Kent School, Yale, Harvard, and Johns Hopkins, he earned his doctorate under Helmut Hoffmann by 1959 and taught at the University of Pennsylvania (circa 1948–1982).

Scott A. Mitchell specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the Graduate Theological Union under Richard K. Payne (attested 2008) and held posts at the Institute of Buddhist Studies and the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research.
Scott DeLancey (born 1949) is a linguist and Tibetologist who studied under Yungdrung Manang. He held a post at the University of Oregon circa 1982.

Scott Hurley is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He studied under Elizabeth Harrison, earned his PhD from the University of Arizona in 2001, and became an associate professor at Luther College in 2002.

Scott Pacey specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. After earning his doctorate from the Australian National University in 2011, he held posts at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, the University of Manchester, and the Australian National University.

Sean D. Gaffney specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at SOAS University of London under Tadeusz Skorupski, Philip Denwood, Renate Söhnen-Thieme, Alexander Piatigorsky, and David Seyfort Ruegg, completing his PhD and holding an attested post there.

Sebastian Nehrdich is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Kyoto University, the University of Hamburg, and the University of Düsseldorf. He has held positions at Hamburg, Düsseldorf, Tohoku University, and the University of California, Berkeley.
Sebastian Pole works in Indology and related fields. He completed his education at the East West College of Herbalism, the London College of Oriental Medicine, and the College of Ayurveda.

Sebastião Rodolfo Dalgado (1855–1922) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Pontifical Institute of Saint Apollinaris. He served as Professor de Sânscrito at Curso Superior de Letras (1907) and Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Lisbon (1917).
See Mui Yian specializes in Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Hong Kong under the supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2010).

Seema Alavi (born 1961) is a historian who completed her doctorate at the University of Cambridge (circa 1986–1991). She has held teaching and professorial posts at Jawaharlal Nehru University, Jamia Millia Islamia, the University of Delhi, and Ashoka University.

Seigai Omura (1868–1927) worked in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied at Tokyo University of the Arts under Umpei Shinma and Kanō Tomonobu, later serving there as assistant professor (1896) and professor (1905), and founded Bussho Kankōkai.

Seiichi Mizuno (1905–1971) was a scholar of history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Kyoto University under Kosaku Hamada, he served there at the Institute for Research in Humanities and as professor from 1949 to 1968.

Seiichi Yagi (born 1932) is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. After studying at the University of Tokyo (circa 1951–1955), he held posts at the Tokyo Institute of Technology (circa 1968–1989), Kanto Gakuin University, and Toin University of Yokohama.

Seiichiro Ono (1891–1986) was a scholar of law, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. Educated at the First Higher School and the University of Tokyo, he served as an assistant professor (1919) and professor (1922–1951) at Tokyo, and later at Aichi Gakuin University (1957–1977).
Seiji Kimura works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Komazawa University and later held posts there (attested 1990) and as a lecturer at Komazawa Junior College (attested 1995).
Seiji Kumagai (born 1980) specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Kyoto University (circa 2005–2008) and became a professor there circa 2013.

Seiji Nemoto (born 1949) specializes in Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Meiji University (circa 1968–1978) and served as a professor at the University of Tsukuba (circa 2003–2015).
Seiji Tanaka (1897–1994) studied under Bruno Petzold. He later held posts at Aoyama Gakuin University (circa 1968–1978) and Asia University (circa 1978–1987).
